_comment: The Risen's villain (Expansion 6 D.3, docs/ADVENTURES.md §6.2): the dead king, proud or grieving; his moves (an omen, a letter in an old hand, his dead at the camp's edge by night, a test on the road) and his boss template (phase two: the barrow wakes).

first_words: "Kneel," says {villain}, in a voice like a door in a tomb. "I was a king before your grandfathers' grandfathers were born."
"Do you know what you stand on?" says {villain}. "My hall. My floor. You are here by my leave, and my leave is withdrawn."
"You smell of the field and the road," says {villain_short}. "Of labour. Cattle always do. Come, then, and be driven."
"I gave this country its law," says {villain}. "What have your kind given it? Mud, and a grave to be dug."
"A flesh thing with a blade," says {villain_short}, and almost smiles. "My hounds would have done better. Come, then."
"Bend the knee, and I will have you buried with honour," says {villain}. "Refuse, and I will have you buried."
"I have been dead longer than {town} has had a name," says {villain_short}. "Do not suppose you are the first to try."
omens: A crown of twisted grass lies in the road, set down with care, as if for someone to find.
A line of old iron spearheads stands upright in the verge, each driven to the socket, all pointing towards the hill.
Every bird on the road has stopped singing. A single raven sits on a milestone with its head turned to the barrow.
The frost in the ruts has made a pattern like a crown, and the sun has been on it for an hour and has not touched it.
A cairn has been built at the roadside overnight, the biggest stone set at the top, and a bone hand lies on it, palm up, as if asking for tribute.
A banner of rotted purple hangs from a dead tree. There is no wind, and still it stirs.
The milestones along the road have been turned in the night, so that their faces look towards the hill.
An old coin stamped with a face no one living remembers has been laid on every gatepost for a mile.
Hoofprints run up the road, a whole troop's worth, and end in the middle of a field. There are no horses anywhere.
A ring of bones kneels in the long grass, all of them facing the barrow, all with their heads bowed.

first_words: "They buried me under the hill and forgot my name," says {villain}. "You will remember it."
"It was so quiet in the hill," says {villain_short}. "So long. Nobody came. Why did nobody come?"
"My hall is a barrow," says {villain}, "and my people are bones in a field. You will forgive me if I do not welcome you."
"I was betrayed at my own table," says {villain_short}, "by one I loved. I have had a great many years to think of it."
"Do not pity me," says {villain}. "I would take it as an insult, and I have little left but my insults."
"I only wanted to see my country once more," says {villain_short}. "And you would take even that from me."
"Everything I knew is gone," says {villain}. "{town} is built on the road where my riders went. You live on my grave."
omens: Someone has set a ring of white stones round an old grave by the road, and the grass inside it is dead.
A bunch of dried flowers lies on a cairn at the crossroads. Every petal is the colour of ash, and the stems are bound with black thread.
The lip of the old well is wet, though no one has drawn water in days, and the cold coming up from it is a grave's cold.
A child's shoe sits on a milestone, set there carefully, as though someone were expected to come back for it.
The dead grass lies flat along a stretch of the road as though someone knelt there for a very long time, and at the end of it is the print of a single knee.
A moth-eaten cloak hangs on a thorn, folded neatly over the branch, and on the cloth is a stain that might be wine or might be blood.
A low sound comes over the fields at dusk, like singing without words, and the animals will not go forward until it stops.
The dust of the road has been written in with a finger: one name, over and over, that no one on the road can read.
A wooden toy horse lies in the middle of the road with its face turned to the barrow.
The hedge along the barrow road is white with frost in high summer, and the frost lies in the shape of hands pressing out.

lines: A cold hand lifts, and all round the hall the lids of the sarcophagi grind and slide. The barrow is waking.
Stone lids crack along the walls, and from every coffin in the hall a pale hand reaches up. The dead are answering the call.
A voice that is not a voice rings through the hall, and the sarcophagi shudder and open. The guard of the dead rises to defend the throne.
Dust sifts from the roof. All along the hall old bones draw themselves together and stand, and the cold in the air turns sharp as a knife.
